## About this page

Where copies of your vault go, how often they are made, and how to save or merge one by hand.

#### Why it is there

A vault kept on one device is lost with that device. A copy somewhere else is how you get it back after a theft, a broken disk or a wipe password.

#### How it works

A backup is the encrypted vault file itself. It holds every vault on this device, nested vaults and attachments included, without showing how many there are. Only your password opens it, so it can sit on a server you do not trust.

[Where they go](/guide/settings/backup/#group-backup-places) lists your places. [How often](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-schedule) makes copies on its own, [How many to keep](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-keep) limits them, and [Save a file](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-save-file) and [Merge a file](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-merge-file) work by hand.

#### When to use it

Set up at least one place soon after you make your vault, somewhere other than this device.

See also [Places for copies](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-places), [Sync and accounts](/guide/settings/sync/), [The vault file](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-vault-file).

<a id="group-backup-places"></a>

## Where they go

The places that receive a copy each time a backup runs.

#### How it works

Each row shows when the last copy was made there, or what went wrong.

The backup button on a row makes a copy there now. Click the row itself to bring back a copy, change its details or stop using it.

Changing the details of an account place lets you keep its current sign-in, so you do not have to sign in again.

See also [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place), [Back up now](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-now), [Bring back a copy](/guide/settings/backup/#action-restore-copy), [Places for copies](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-places).

<a id="action-backup-now"></a>

## Back up now

Makes a copy at this place now, outside the schedule.

#### How it works

WM Pass writes the new copy, reads it back, compares it with what it sent and checks that it is a WM Pass backup. Only then does it remove the oldest copies beyond [How many to keep](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-keep).

A run that fails part way can leave one copy too many, never one too few.

#### Limits

Any place but a folder needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed).

See also [How many to keep](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-keep), [Bring back a copy](/guide/settings/backup/#action-restore-copy).

<a id="action-add-place"></a>

## Add a place

Sets up somewhere new to keep copies: a folder, an account, a server, a Git repository or a mailbox.

#### How it works

Choose the kind, give it a name and fill in what that kind needs. A backup runs as soon as it is saved, so you know at once whether it works.

Only the encrypted file goes there. What WM Pass needs to sign in stays on this device, sealed.

- A folder on this device. Syncthing, Nextcloud or a cloud provider's own app can carry it on from there.
- With Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and Box you sign in on the service's own page, in your browser. WM Pass never sees that password, and can reach only its own folder there. Google Drive can use a hidden app folder or a folder you can see.
- With pCloud, MEGA and Proton Drive you sign in here, with a code afterwards if the account asks for one. WM Pass keeps the session the sign-in hands back, not your password.
- With iCloud Drive you sign in here, and Apple asks for a code from one of your devices. The sign-in lasts about a month, then WM Pass asks again.
- For WebDAV, such as Nextcloud, pick a service to have the address filled in, or type it.
- For S3, such as Backblaze or MinIO, pick a service for its endpoint and regions, or type the endpoint.
- SFTP signs in with a password or an OpenSSH private key. The server's key is remembered on the first connection, and if it ever changes WM Pass refuses to connect.
- FTP and SMB reach a server, or a Windows or Samba share.
- NFS reaches an export on your network. NFS without Kerberos takes the user and group ids on trust and does not encrypt, so use it only on a network you control.
- Synology and QNAP reach a NAS through its own file manager.
- Git keeps copies in a folder of a private repository on GitHub, GitLab or Gitea (which also covers Forgejo and Codeberg), with an access token. Each copy is a commit.
- Email keeps copies in a mailbox, over IMAP. Each copy is one message.

#### Limits

Saving any place but a folder turns on [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed), since reaching it is the reason you set it up.

Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and Box are offered only by builds made with an app id for that service.

#### On Android

Any place but a folder needs [Allow network features](/guide/settings/security/#setting-network-allowed). Until it is on, a backup there stops and says network features are turned off.

Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and Box are offered only by builds made with an app id for that service.

See also [Path-style addresses](/guide/settings/backup/#action-place-path-style), [Encrypt the connection](/guide/settings/backup/#action-place-ftp-encrypt), [Require encryption](/guide/settings/backup/#action-place-smb-encrypt), [Accept the NAS’s own certificate](/guide/settings/backup/#action-place-nas-certificate), [Allow a public repository](/guide/settings/backup/#action-place-git-public), [Places for copies](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-places).

<a id="action-place-path-style"></a>

## Path-style addresses

Puts the bucket name in the path of each address, as endpoint/bucket/file, rather than in the host name, as bucket.endpoint/file.

#### How it works

The switch appears only when you type the endpoint yourself. Picking a service from the list sets this for you.

#### When to use it

Turn it on for MinIO, Garage, or a server you reach by its IP address, which have no host name for each bucket.

See also [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place).

<a id="action-place-ftp-encrypt"></a>

## Encrypt the connection

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Uses TLS on an FTP connection, so the server's password crosses the network encrypted.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | TLS starts before the sign-in, and the password and the file travel inside it. |
| Off | Plain FTP. The password crosses the network as text. Turn this off only for an old server that offers nothing else. |

#### Limits

With it off, anyone who can watch the network can read the password and then delete or replace your copies on that server. The vault inside them stays encrypted either way.

See also [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place).

<a id="action-place-smb-encrypt"></a>

## Require encryption

*Only in the desktop app and Android.*

Requires SMB 3 encryption for everything after the sign-in, and refuses a server that cannot do it.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | The file and everything else after the sign-in cross the network encrypted. |
| Off | An older server that stops at SMB 2 can sign the traffic without encrypting it. The file crosses the network as plain bytes, though it is the encrypted vault. |

See also [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place).

<a id="action-place-nas-certificate"></a>

## Accept the NAS’s own certificate

Lets WM Pass connect to a Synology or QNAP NAS whose certificate it made itself, which no known authority vouches for.

#### Why it is there

Most NAS boxes on a home network answer with a certificate of their own. Without this switch, WM Pass refuses it.

#### How it works

The first certificate seen is remembered. A later connection that shows a different one is refused, the same rule as an SFTP server's key.

#### Limits

If you replace the NAS's certificate, WM Pass refuses the new one too. Remove the place and add it again.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Accept the NAS's own certificate.

See also [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place).

<a id="action-place-git-public"></a>

## Allow a public repository

Lets WM Pass write copies to a repository anyone can see. With it off, WM Pass checks the repository first and refuses a public one.

#### Why it is there

Each copy is a commit, and a repository's history keeps every file ever written, deleted or not. In a public repository, anyone could download every copy you ever made.

#### Limits

Only your password opens those copies, but anyone could keep them and try to guess the password offline, with no limit on attempts. A private repository is safer.

See also [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place).

<a id="action-restore-copy"></a>

## Bring back a copy

Lists the copies at this place, newest first, and merges the one you choose into this vault.

#### How it works

Merging does not replace what you have. Where an item differs, the newer value wins and the older one goes into that item's history. A copy of some other vault does not open under this key, and nothing changes.

#### Limits

Only the 30 newest copies are listed.

See also [Merge a file](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-merge-file), [Where they go](/guide/settings/backup/#group-backup-places).

<a id="action-place-stop"></a>

## Stop using it

Forgets this place and its login on this device. Copies already there stay where they are.

#### Limits

To remove those copies, delete them at the place itself.

See also [Where they go](/guide/settings/backup/#group-backup-places).

<a id="action-backup-schedule"></a>

## How often

Makes a copy at every place on its own, every day or every week.

#### How it works

Scheduled copies run while the vault is locked too, since they only move the encrypted file. The newest copy is read back and checked before any older one is removed.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| By hand | Copies are made only when you choose the backup button on a place. |
| Every day | One copy a day at each place. |
| Every week | One copy a week at each place. |

#### Limits

WM Pass has to be running. With [Keep running in the tray](/guide/settings/desktop/#setting-close-to-tray) on, closing the window keeps it going. If a copy was due while WM Pass was not running, it is made soon after WM Pass starts.

#### On Android

Android makes the copy in the background, without the app open. The system picks the moment, and waits while the battery is low.

See also [How many to keep](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-keep), [Back up now](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-now).

<a id="action-backup-keep"></a>

## How many to keep

How many copies stay at each place. Once a new copy has been checked, the oldest beyond this number are removed.

#### Limits

The count covers every WM Pass backup at that place, so two devices backing up to the same place share it.

Files that are not named as WM Pass backups are never touched, so the place can hold other things.

See also [How often](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-schedule), [Back up now](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-now).

<a id="action-backup-save-file"></a>

## Save a file

Saves a backup file wherever you choose, such as a USB stick.

#### How it works

It is the same encrypted bundle a place receives, and it opens with your vault's password.

#### When to use it

Before a big change, or to keep a copy that is never online.

See also [Merge a file](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-merge-file), [The vault file](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-vault-file).

<a id="action-backup-merge-file"></a>

## Merge a file

Merges a backup file or a vault file into the vault that is open.

#### How it works

Where an item differs, the newer value is kept and the older one moves to that item's history. A file that holds some other vault, under another key, changes nothing.

#### When to use it

To bring back items from an old backup, or to combine a copy that was changed on a device that was not syncing.

See also [Bring back a copy](/guide/settings/backup/#action-restore-copy), [Save a file](/guide/settings/backup/#action-backup-save-file).

<a id="action-place-from-keyboard"></a>

## Use a place from WM Keyboard

*Only in Android.*

Fills in a new place with one you already set up in WM Keyboard, so its address and password are typed only once.

#### How it works

Under [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place), press **Use a place from WM Keyboard**. WM Keyboard opens its list of places, behind its own app lock if you set one, and you tap one.

The place fills in the sheet here. Look it over and save it. Nothing is kept until you do, and then it is sealed like any other place.

A login a server checks comes across whole: a WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, SMB, email or NAS password, an SFTP key, an S3 key pair, a Git token.

A sign-in does not. Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and Box sign each app in separately, and a token from one does nothing in the other. Box and Proton Drive replace their tokens on every use, so two apps sharing one would sign each other out, and pCloud, MEGA and iCloud Drive keep sessions too. For those you sign in here.

A folder on this phone comes without the folder, since Android lets an app into a folder only when you pick it there. A folder inside an account that still has WM Keyboard's default name becomes WM Pass's default.

WM Keyboard can borrow one of your places the same way. It opens a page here that waits until the vault is open, lists your places, and sends only the one you tap.

#### Limits

Each app answers only the other, checked by its signing certificate. The place goes straight from one app's memory to the other's, never through a file or the clipboard.

Each app keeps its own copy. Changing or removing the place in one leaves the other alone.

See also [Add a place](/guide/settings/backup/#action-add-place), [Places for copies](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-places), [Let WM Keyboard fill](/guide/settings/security/#setting-keyboard-access).
